author: New China TV
description:
In 1999, American teacher Ronald Sakolsky raised and donated 5,000 USD to support Chinese farmer Yin Yuzhen's fight against desertification in Ordos, Inner Mongolia.
That act of kindness took root in the once-barren land. Today, tens of thousands of trees stand there, forming a forest that bears Sakolsky's name.
On Aug. 24, travelling across the Pacific to see changes of this once-barren land, Sakolsky drew a tree on the tablet, and filled a small bottle of soil.
Why does he want to carry this piece of earth all the way home to Pittsburgh?
title: A bottle of sand from Inner Mongolia: A piece of China, a jar of love

author: New China TV
description:
In 2000, American teacher Ronald Sakolsky traveled to the Maowusu Sandy Land in Ordos, Inner Mongolia, to visit Chinese farmer Yin Yuzhen. A year earlier, moved by her determination to combat desertification, he raised and donated 5,000 USD to support her tree-planting efforts. During that first visit, they planted a tree together, as a small promise to the future.
With the help of media, Yin finally reconnected with Sakolsky this May and invited him back to see what had become of the land they once knew.
On Aug. 24, 26 years after his first visit, Sakolsky returned. The tree he and Yin had planted now towered several times above their heads. His act of kindness reaching across the Pacific has also grown into an entire forest. 
What did this return mean to him, and what had this journey taught him about hope, perseverance and the power of working together?
title: Across the Pacific, a seed of kindness became a forest
